hypothese.summary: Q2 2026 in line with management's expectations (EPS 1,37$ beats consensus by 2,2%, revenue slightly misses by 0,4%): comp sales -1,0% (sequential improvement vs -1,7% in Q1, consistent with guidance). hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Sprouts is a unit-growth + buyback compounder in specialty grocery. Q2 2026 tracked the setup path: comps -1.0% (sequential improvement from -1.7%, as guided), EPS 1.37 beating consensus +2.2% - but the beat is INTEGRALLY buyback-driven: EBIT and net slightly declined YoY, with diluted shares down 4.4%. Guidance: revenue raised (+5.5/6.5%), yet EBIT and EPS CEILINGS lowered - margin pressure is real while the top line holds.

== THESIS READ ==
- The EPS algorithm currently runs on the share count, not operating growth - acceptable transitionally, not durably. Watch: EBIT growth turning positive again (H2 comparisons ease).
- Comps recovery is on the guided glide path (-1.7% -> -1.0% -> guided -0.5/+0.5% FY). Watch: traffic vs basket split in Q3.
- Unit growth intact (42 new stores FY26, capex at top of range) - the long-term engine. Watch: new-store productivity cohort data.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
53rd week in FY2026: revenue +200M, EBIT +28M, EPS +0.21 - the 2027 comparison base must be RETREATED to 52-week equivalent before applying organic growth (documented at setup, reconfirmed). GAAP basis throughout; net cash eroding to slightly net debt by 2029 as buybacks outrun FCF.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
FY26: revenue ~9,534M (guidance mid + 53rd week), EBIT ~708M, EPS ~5.57. 2027-2030: ~6%/yr organic on the 52-week base, EBIT margin 7.7% -> 8.6%, ETR 25.5% (guided), shares -2.5%/yr. Bridge trivial (near-zero finNet). Watch: the guidance-ceiling cuts as an early margin-pressure signal; competitive intensity in fresh/natural.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Oct/Nov); comps inflection to positive; FY27 guidance (Feb) on the retreated 52-week base.

ancrages.moteur: A pipeline of more than 110 executed leases and 155 approved stores (vs ~150/105+ at creation, improving) supports 42 net new stores in FY26 (a quarterly record of 15+ openings expected in Q3 alone). REINFORCED this refresh: the last 4 store cohorts ALL comp positively (new data point confirmed in Q2), and the cannibalisation observed is currently at the low end of the historical 100-150bp range - a signal that the pipeline remains a healthy structural driver of revenue beyond the comp.

Maturation of the new stores and self-distribution (meat now in ~85% of stores via the new Northern California DC, with cautious extension to other private-label categories mentioned over several years) support gradual operating leverage on the EBIT margin beyond 2026. Trajectory revised slightly lower vs creation (7,7%->8,6% over 2027-2030 instead of 7,8%->8,7%), given the FY26 EPS guidance narrowed with a lowered ceiling (unbudgeted fuel costs).

A 1 Md$ share buyback authorisation (626 M$ remaining after 210 M$ already used in H1 26, of which 70 M$ in Q2 alone) funds a reduction in the diluted share count of about 2,5%/yr - the CFO confirms a target of at least 300 M$ of buybacks for the full year (already 210 M$ in H1, so at least a further 90 M$ expected in H2). Consistent with the pace observed since 2015. The Q2 EPS increase (+1,5%) despite EBIT and net income SLIGHTLY DOWN concretely illustrates this mechanism.

CONFIRMED IDENTICALLY this refresh by the official Q2 2026 release: the 53rd fiscal week (Q4 26) adds a one-off roughly 200 M$ of revenue, 28 M$ of EBIT and 0,21$ of diluted EPS above the FY26 guidance explicitly communicated on a 52-week basis - no divergence from the creation assumption. This effect does not recur in 2027, which mechanically compresses the reported revenue growth the following year if it is not adjusted (see PARAMETERS).
Normative effective tax rate taken at 25,5%, explicitly confirmed by the official FY26 guidance published at Q2 (the actual effective rate for Q2 alone was 26%, close to the annual guidance).

NEW ANCHOR this refresh: a Cyclospora episode affecting lettuce/salads across the sector, very recent (the last 2 weeks before the call), no recall at Sprouts to date. Impact judged modest by the CFO (below one analyst's estimate of 80-120bp), but duration and magnitude still uncertain at the time of the call. Not quantified and not incorporated into adjXXX - a pure downside risk for Q3 2026, to be monitored explicitly at the next refresh.

epsAdj.basisNote: GAAP - a beat of 2,2%, but entirely driven by the decline in the diluted share count (-4,4% year on year): EBIT (174,2 M$) and net income (129,2 M$) are both SLIGHTLY DOWN year on year (-2,9% and -3,4% respectively). Revenue slightly missed consensus (-0,4%).

epsReported.note: GAAP diluted EPS of $1.37 (+1% YoY) on GAAP net income of $129.2M (down 3.4% YoY) and EBIT of $174.2M (down 2.9% YoY); the per-share growth comes entirely from the 4.4% YoY reduction in diluted shares. Verified against stockanalysis.com quarterly financials (quarter ended June 28, 2026).

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: Q3 26: comp sales -0.5% to +1.5%; diluted EPS $1.20-$1.24. EBIT margin pressure of roughly -50bp expected (fixed-cost deleverage on softer comps plus a higher store-opening count than Q3 2025), with a P&L shape similar to Q2 (gross margin and SG&A both slightly negative, additional D&A pressure); Q3 also absorbs a little fuel and a little Cyclospora impact per the CFO. At least 15 new stores planned in Q3 - the highest quarterly opening cadence in company history. July already tracking slightly negative, within the guidance range.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 (52-week basis, 53rd week at the end of Q4): total sales growth raised to +5.5%/+6.5% (from +4.5%/+6.5%), comps narrowed and improved to -0.5%/+0.5% (from -1%/+1%), EBIT $675-685M (ceiling cut from $695M), diluted EPS $5.32-$5.40 (ceiling cut from $5.48) assuming at least $300M of buybacks, net capex ~$310M (top of prior range), 42 net new stores (43 openings less one closure of an underperforming store at lease expiry), effective tax rate ~25.5%. The CFO attributes the entire ~$5M EBIT midpoint delta to unhedged, unbudgeted H2 fuel costs ($2.5M per quarter); Q4 gross margin expected up slightly on the one-time loyalty-program cycling ($2 to $1 threshold) and an easier shrink compare.
pointsCles: CEO Jack Sinclair states the toughest year-over-year comparisons are now behind: June was the worst month of the quarter (lapping 2025's exceptional produce season and the natural/organic supply-chain disruption that had pushed traffic to Sprouts), and July has already returned in line with expectations, tracking slightly negative within the Q3 guidance range.

The +2.2% EPS beat is entirely buyback-driven: EBIT ($174.2M, -2.9% YoY) and GAAP net income ($129.2M, -3.4% YoY) both declined slightly, with diluted shares down 4.4% - a caution flag against a superficial reading of the 'beat'. Gross margin 38.7% (-12bp, loyalty investment plus unbudgeted fuel), SG&A deleverage -30bp.

The structural unit-growth engine remains intact: 490 stores across 25 states, pipeline of 110+ executed leases and 155 approved sites, the last four store vintages all comping positive, cannibalization at the low end of the historical 100-150bp range, and a new fast-densification playbook for new markets (Chicago targeted at 10 stores within 12-18 months from 2027).

Emerging near-term risk: an industry-wide Cyclospora episode on lettuce/salads felt over the last two weeks of July (no Sprouts product recall; shift from fresh to frozen observed), with impact called smaller than Evercore's 80-120bp estimate but not precisely quantified; a one-time Q4 gross-margin tailwind is explicitly identified (loyalty threshold cycled from $2 to $1 since January 2026, plus an easier shrink comparison).

hypothese.guidanceLongTerme: No quantified target beyond FY2026 formally communicated. Qualitative direction: a return to 'the algorithm' of growth once the difficult comparisons are behind (implicitly, a positive comp supported by the store pipeline and the continued improvement in traffic/units). Planned geographic expansion including Chicago from 2027 (target of 10 stores in 12-18 months).

guidanceScorecard.paceCheckpoint: Q2 real: EPS 1.37 beat consensus +2.2% - but EBIT and net DECLINED YoY; the entire EPS growth comes from the -4.4% diluted share count. Comps -1.0% improving sequentially from -1.7%.

annualBeatHistory.note: Initial FY25 guidance (Q4-2024 release, 20/02/2025): adjusted diluted EPS 4.52-4.68$ (mid 4.60), comps +4.5/6.5%; realized 5.31$ (comps +7.3%) - level +15.4%, a second consecutive outsized beat year.

Initial FY24 guidance (Q4-2023 release, Feb 2024): adjusted diluted EPS 2.85-2.95$ (mid 2.90); realized 3.75$ (comps +7.6%) - level +29.3%: the guidance was set before the traffic inflection and never caught up.
